walkthroughs.body_html: Antarctica holds ~70% of Earth's freshwater in its ice sheets; its 14 million km² surface is roughly 98% ice-covered. Coastal stations may exceed 0 °C in summer; the interior plateau routinely sees below -60 °C. Katabatic winds and the circumpolar current isolate the continent.

Despite extremes, the Southern Ocean is highly productive. Krill (Euphausia superba) supports whales, crabeater seals and penguins. Endemic mosses, lichens and limited terrestrial invertebrates persist. Emperor penguins endure -50 °C winters to breed on sea ice.

The 1959 Antarctic Treaty froze territorial claims, banned military activity, demilitarised the continent and committed parties to scientific cooperation. The 1991 Madrid Protocol prohibits mineral extraction (subject to review from 2048) and establishes environmental impact assessment requirements. Climate change is now the most serious threat.
